mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO contraction below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL are above their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive divergence between real personal income (implied from PAYEMS and CPIAUCSL) and real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over three months signals a buildup of household savings, which typically precedes a delayed consumption rebound and a positive equity market reaction over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Real income outpaces real consumption for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when real income outpaces consumption for three months in a post-recession recovery.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS grows above 0.5% MoM for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above its 12-month MA for six consecutive months.
